hits.name: Ethan Mollick
hits.text:
One ongoing frustration is the lack of effort I see being put towards near-term, achievable crash projects to do good with AI at a national scale, whether those efforts are by the AI labs or by policymakers & NGOs.

Some obvious ideas to explore suggested by the data we have so far: universal tutoring to support classroom learning, second opinions on healthcare, financial literacy/scam avoidance, and making government services easy to access.

These are hard problems, and I know because over the past 20 years I have worked extensively on building tutoring and financial literacy programs, which were always limited by existing technology. Now, real gains are likely achievable with AI, which should be a big deal. Yes, you would want to do careful design and studies before rolling things out. And yes, those efforts might fail. But, if done right, national programs could lead to big gains in public good for seemingly intractable problems. And they don't require AIs beyond current models to pull off.

virals.name: Rimsha Bhardwaj
virals.text:
GitHub is hiding some INSANE video editing tools for Claude Code and Codex.

I found 10 repos that can help automate cuts, captions, animations, and repetitive editing work.

Bookmark this:

1. FFmpeg Skill

Give your coding agent 42 local editing tools for cuts, captions, audio cleanup, reframing, overlays, and platform exports.

https://t.co/p3SyJBzvxn

2. Herk Edit Kit

Nate Herk’s editing kit for Claude Code and Codex. Cut dead air, edit from transcripts, and add captions and motion graphics using HyperFrames templates.

https://t.co/MfmKIQoZ7u

3. OpenChatCut

Connect Claude Code or Codex to a real video-editing timeline through MCP. Describe your changes, preview the proposed edit, and approve it.

https://t.co/utEGOA4Pgr

4. Remotion Agent Skills

Official skills that help AI agents create animated title cards, captions, transitions, and entire video compositions with React.

https://t.co/InZhZVTMwW

5. Auto-Editor

Automate your first rough cut by removing silent sections. Adjust the padding around cuts to keep the pacing natural.

https://t.co/2DNwFgdzIk

6. FireRed-OpenStoryline

An AI editing agent with natural-language instructions, reusable editing styles, and built-in Claude Code skills. Codex support is experimental.

https://t.co/maktqr5Sk8

7. Motion Video Kit

Give Claude Code workflows for launch videos, animated product demos, and motion graphics, including sound design and visual review.

https://t.co/M8oOPqS5or

8. Stable-ts

Generate subtitles with word-level timestamps using Whisper. Export SRT, VTT, or ASS captions through a command-line workflow your agent can run.

https://t.co/Zs9HxBC4OA

9. PySceneDetect

Automatically detect scene changes, split footage into clips, and extract preview frames. Useful for organizing long recordings before editing.

https://t.co/NDeSD4LdF4

10. Editly

Turn a JSON or JavaScript edit plan into a finished video. Combine footage, images, titles, transitions, and music for repeatable batch edits.

https://t.co/Rx48ccKx7b

Some connect directly through skills or MCP. Others give your agent command-line tools to run. Setup and any model or rendering costs vary.

What did I miss?

virals.name: Mark Kretschmann
virals.text:
One of the people behind Claude Code's rise is joining OpenAI. Cat Wu, @AnthropicAI's former Claude Code product lead, announced today that she'll lead product management for OpenAI's Core Products. She helped take Claude Code from a small internal tool to a major commercial product and also oversaw Cowork, Anthropic's agent for non-coding work.

Her new role extends beyond coding. Business Insider reports she'll work with Nick Turley on enterprise products and Ashley Alexander on consumer products, reporting to Tibo Sottiaux. OpenAI is getting someone who has already helped turn an experimental coding agent into a tool developers use every day, just as it pushes to get more businesses using Codex.

ideas.title: Keep agent history forever or prune it?

x_keywords.method: Read-only x MCP search_posts_all, 2 calls per keyword: last 24 h and previous 24 h (24-48 h ago); lang:en, no retweets/replies, sort=relevancy, up to 25 posts per window. This is a SAMPLE of top-relevance posts, not every post on X. Views = impression_count at fetch time. Rank = sum of sampled 24 h views; 48 h = both windows; trend = 24 h sum / previous 24 h sum (up >=1.3, down <=0.7). Fresh posts are still gaining views, so 'up' is understated. Top-post share > 70% means one viral post carries the keyword.

trend_radar.legend: Trend match 0-100% = 1 - prod(1 - w) over matched 24 h keywords that another author also used in the 48 h window (w: rank 1-10 0.35, 11-25 0.22, 26-40 0.12, curated 0.20). Verdict: >= 50% -> trend; else video/image in the post data -> visual; else >= 100K followers (outsiders without follower data: >= 500K views, estimate) -> author/audience; else coincidence/other. Missing data shows as 'no data'. Heat = sum log10(views) of topic posts (24 h x1, 24-48 h x0.5), scaled to 100. Momentum = log-views last 24 h / previous 24 h. Trend-input-only accounts feed the corpus but are never shown as hits.
